item.title: Nex 2.6.17
item.description: Larger files, clear refusals. Ordinary attachments now allow 500 MB; oversized or unreadable selections explain why they were not imported. Untagged appears only when useful. The filter hides when every timeline note has tags and clears an empty active selection. Undo keeps its promise. Permanent trash deletion waits until its Undo actually closes, and AI edits keep an Undo button in compact editors. Capture preserves unsaved work. Failed writes stop media handoff; failed conversions keep the original reminder and retry without duplicating the converted note. Reminder taps survive the lock. Recurring reminders open their destination after unlocking. Editing continues at the end. Notes, captions and attachment captions open with the caret after the existing text. Assistant answers use real library totals. Counts come from the database; internal searches stay out of replies and interrupted cloud answers get one bounded retry. Bottom navigation is easier to see. A subtle outline and a distinct background separate the dock from content in Light, Dark and Night. Navigation returns quietly after capture. Closing capture restores the dock without the rotation and zoom animation. Restore checks compatibility before changing your library. Older supported libraries are upgraded on a temporary copy; incompatible or malformed backups leave the current library untouched. Interrupted restores keep a recovery path. Library, media and full-backup settings can return to the previous state; cleanup failures after a successful restore no longer report failure or stop the app opening. A healthy backup can repair missing files. Missing photos in the current library no longer prevent restoration, and the safety copy records which files were already missing. Backup files keep their meaning when shared. A library backup renamed to .zip is recognized, and shared rescue backups retain their missing-file report. Invalid appearance settings are rejected before installation.

item.title: Nex 2.6.16
item.description: An Undo can no longer be swallowed silently. A plain banner arriving while an actionable one is still up waits its turn instead of eating it — and a banner replaced by a newer one leaves through the edge it came from, with its exit animation. Banners keep their own time. They arrive in half the time they used to, their words are readable from the first third of the entrance, the countdown starts once the entrance is over, scales with the message's length, and holding a banner pauses it. Sending a note reads as success. The capture sheet leaves as soon as the words are settled — the timeline reloads behind the closing animation — and the send button becomes a ✓ rather than greying the sheet out like a failure. The first keystroke changes no sizes. Paste keeps its column with only its icon fading, and the schedule hint waits for the words to be still, so nothing jumps around under the arriving keyboard. Paste shows when there is something to paste. The sheet asks — without reading the clipboard — on open and on return, so an empty clipboard no longer shows a button that visibly does nothing. A link's Open sits on the toolbar. Each note kind's primary action — Open for links and files, Edit for text — takes the first slot by rank, not by matching translated labels, which is why Open always used to hide behind More. Long notes open the editor full screen. Past about eight lines the editor owns the screen from the start instead of a 220px box, and ✕ and ✓ are its controls in either size. Pickers arrive like the rest of the app. The time and date pickers rise and settle on the app's own beat and scrim rather than Flutter's flat 150ms fade, and the assistant's settings sheet is the app's own sheet again. The camera's wait is spoken. While the sensor is being asked for, the panel shows a faint skeleton and says what it is doing — and six seconds in it offers the phone's camera app, before the timeout does. Covered, not cleared. Pulling the shade over the vault lays a blur across it and comes straight back with the form as it was — words, caret and place — instead of rebuilding it from a draft; being away past the grace period still locks. The assistant hold hint gets a button. "Got it" is a real button now rather than part of the sentence, and the hint keeps to the app's own label style — still shown only when the assistant can actually answer. A toast leaves the way it arrived. Its content's exit — a small settle and fade on the exit token — completes the entrance it always had. A cut preview says so. A multiline bilingual preview that runs out of rows ends in an ellipsis instead of reading as the note's ending, and blank lines are no longer spent from the budget. A fast retreat is not a flick. Pulling back through the middle to cancel a capture flick no longer fires the opposite side's shortcut; the opposite side still works by crossing its full arm. The wide-window scale is said out loud. Appearance now notes that a wide window draws everything at 90% of the chosen size — the factor was always there, silently, on the notes' own text too. One clearance rule for the dock. A single helper reserves the capture dock's room instead of the same sum written out screen by screen, and the dock itself gives way under an open keyboard. Chosen Night hands over in black. With Night chosen, the window between the system splash and the app's first frame is painted black instead of flashing Soft Dark's grey.

item.title: Nex 2.6.14
item.description: Working tag filters in search. The Tags row finally appears in the search filter sheet, typing tag: finds your tags, and several chosen tags now mean "any of them" — the same as the timeline's filter chips. An honest Undo in the trash. Leaving the trash after deleting a note for good no longer leaves an Undo banner that cannot bring it back. Reading an AI answer or a translation no longer closes the note. Scrolling a long result inside its box stays inside the box, instead of taking the whole sheet with it. Delete works from a recurring item's linked notes. Deleting a linked note there now moves it to the trash with an Undo, instead of quietly doing nothing. A friendlier link capture. Pasting text that is not an address no longer dead-ends: Send keeps it as the note it already is and says so, a Clear button appears, and the "not a link" hint waits until you stop typing. The back gesture keeps a recording in progress. Leaving the recording sheet the way Android goes back now keeps the recording — the same as Stop — instead of throwing it away.

item.title: Nex 2.6.13
item.description: Faster opening of long notes and text files. The first page appears with the detail sheet instead of waiting for it to finish opening. Smoother reading and actions. Long documents reveal progressively and keep menus and scrolling more responsive; Markdown blocks and whitespace stay intact.

item.title: Nex 2.6.12

Changes to schedules, completion history and attached details still appear, and today's completion counts refresh correctly after midnight. Smoother navigation throughout Nex. Unchanged screens in Threads, Library, Set Aside, note details, Home layout, and Intelligence no longer redraw unnecessarily after returning. Real changes remain visible. Notes, tags, attachments, and thread membership continue to update when edited.

item.title: Nex 2.6.11

item.title: Nex 2.6.10

Older notes keep existing extra tags until you remove them in note details. Imports with more than three distinct tags on a note are rejected before saving any notes, with a clear warning rather than silently discarding tags.

item.title: Nex 2.6.8

Selection and ringing reminders use the same circle; selecting a ringing note acknowledges it without deleting its reminder. More readable navigation and filters. Tag filters show quiet note counts, while the floating navigation bar gets a fine outline and soft shadow. Liquid Glass temporarily paused. The option is disabled while its appearance is refined; the saved selection remains intact.

item.title: Nex 2.6.7

A white page and gentle grey cards make notes easier to scan, without decorative card borders or shadows. Clearer fields and matching Android colours. Text fields keep a slim visible outline; Android launch and home-widget colours follow the new look. Your accent, Liquid Glass and accessibility settings still work.

item.title: Nex 2.6.6

Night keeps the former dark look; System follows your device using the new Dark. Existing dark selections become Night. Custom accents and Liquid Glass remain available. A steady Nex appearance. Preset themes are temporarily unavailable while the main Nex look is refined; their saved choices are kept. Correct note order in threads. Notes stay in chronological order even when their saved timestamps have different precision.

item.title: Nex 2.6.5
item.description: Rescue library backups. Keep recoverable notes and files even when some attachments are missing, with a clear missing-file list. Normal backups keep their complete-file checks. More responsive libraries. Capture stays available during sync network waits, and smart search does less repeated work in large libraries. Card status icons sit closer together with a consistent small bottom gap. Complete private-vault backups. Choosing Include private vault now carries its encrypted photos, recordings and files to the restored device. Large private lists and draft saving are lighter. Safer sync and updates. Unsent conflicting edits are kept as a separate note. Approved interrupted downloads can resume after restarting Nex; store copies continue to update only through their store. File saving and scheduled-note processing are more reliable.

item.title: Nex 2.6.4

Reminder, attachment and urgent icons appear in that order with tiny separate halos that follow the card's press highlight. Reminder times and attachment counts are temporarily hidden on cards; their data and accessible descriptions remain available.

item.title: Nex 2.6.3

item.title: Nex 2.6.2
item.description: Uniform timeline cards. Collapsed notes keep one height across text, photos, links, checklists and voice. Captions use a quieter preview line; reminder, urgent and attachment marks stay together in a separate area without empty slots.

item.title: Nex 2.6.1
item.description: A more useful smart summary. Pending work, reminders and important notes take priority; routine completed habits no longer crowd them out. Calmer capture and easier translation. Paste fades smoothly as its space closes, and the whole translation language bar opens the picker. Steadier timeline cards. Reminder, attachment and urgent marks share the preview space on ordinary collapsed cards, while captions and expanded notes keep their room. Optional assistant Memory. Keep a short introduction behind a separate opt-in, with your existing text preserved. Assistant, smart-summary and Memory settings dim when AI is off. One place for AI request history. What left this device stays under Security and privacy. More selective note summaries. Long explanations are condensed instead of merely reformatted, while short or information-dense notes keep the room their facts need. Reliable quick capture. Notification shortcuts open the right capture tool even when the timeline widget is active. Safer photo editing. Clearing all drawings and text now asks for confirmation before removing your work. Control over assistant reads. Reading Recently Deleted or recurring items for an answer waits for your approval. Clearer selected filters. Selected tag labels remain readable in light, dark and Comfort themes, including custom accents.

item.title: Nex 2.6.0
item.description: Easier photo cropping. Larger touch areas make all four crop handles easier to drag while keeping the visible crop controls in place. A clearer assistant history. Conversations are grouped by time with reply previews and a current-chat indicator. Individual deletion is in each conversation’s menu. A steadier pull to refresh. Reversing your drag closes the refresh strip before the notes scroll. A quiet Nex accent marks success, with separate handling for cancelled and failed refreshes. Find notes without tags. Untagged stays at the end of the tag row and works with note-type and reminder filters. More room to write. The capture clipboard fades away once you start writing and gives its space back to the editor; clearing the text brings it back. Clearer recurring cards. Countdown and exact time sit together, with balanced spacing and centred actions. The check button explicitly marks one occurrence done. Captions for text notes. Add a separate optional caption without replacing the note on its timeline card. Captions are included in search and AI context. Mark what is urgent. Use More Actions or the hold menu to add a small flame. Urgency is independent of Pin and keeps notes in their existing order. Daily nudges without AI. Get brief local reminders based on urgent notes, nearby or recently overdue reminders, unfinished checklists and recurring items. A fresh smart summary is optional; otherwise Nex uses local text, with varied prompts for quiet and empty libraries and at most one daily notification.

item.title: Nex 2.5.4
item.description: Clearer note summaries. More compact summaries better preserve decisions, conditions and figures, with readable formatting and a full expanded view. Safer backup restore. Backups made with an unsupported database format are refused before replacing your library. Markdown that comes back cleanly. Re-imported Nex text and checklist exports keep their dates, tags and titles, without metadata or file IDs appearing as note text. Assistant controls that apply throughout. Image and voice settings also govern media sent from the assistant, including changes made while a chat is open. Less work while you type. Short searches stay local; meaning searches wait for a typing pause and cancel superseded requests. Unrelated settings changes no longer rebuild the app's themes.

item.title: Nex 2.5.3
item.description: A visible summary timestamp. The home summary shows how long ago its last successful AI update was, with minutes and hours and an exact time in its tooltip. Relevant habit settings. The habit-sharing option appears only while Habits is active. Portrait rewrites stay visible. Keep reading the current portrait while its replacement is written; the new text and traits appear on the same page. Useful pinned modules. Compact home cards show local progress, review counts, upcoming occasions, the selected breathing session or cycle information in place of large module names. Still, a quieter theme. Warm neutral surfaces and a soft sage accent, in light and dark. Cards, panels and menus have no decorative borders or shadows; focus and error states remain clear. Clearer Markdown conversion. “Convert to Markdown” distinguishes converting a note inside Nex from saving a file to your device. Open PDF and DOCX with Nex. Choose Nex from Android’s Open with menu to keep and read these documents, just like Markdown files. Know when the next turn is. Recurring cards show a countdown and the exact due date and time alongside daily progress, amounts and snooze status when relevant.

item.title: Nex 2.5.2
item.description: Readable wide tables. Markdown and DOCX tables scroll horizontally with readable column widths, while surrounding text stays within the page. Consistent notifications. Opening Nex keeps module notifications in the notification centre. In-app messages use the top capsule throughout Nex, including Undo and retry actions. Notes stay at the heart of your brief. Preset summaries keep useful note content alongside optional habit progress. Full has room for more topics, and Plain report also includes recent notes without reminders.

item.title: Nex 2.5.1
item.description: Habits in your brief, by choice. Opt in to include relevant habit goals, progress and short statistics in the home summary and daily notification. Switching it off hides previous habit content while keeping the notes summary and independent reminders. Useful habit reminders. See which habit is due, mark a tick done, open an amount's progress form, or ask for a reminder later. Notifications open the right place. Module notifications lead to their item or relevant section, including when Nex was closed, while respecting the app lock. Consistent home AI. Greetings follow the app language even after a failed request. Changing the brief's length or style applies on return from settings, without waiting for the hourly refresh. Better AI editing. Auto style corrects and organises writing. All six tools better preserve meaning and key details; Undo and Save remain under your control. Clearer What's New. Release history focuses on useful features and important fixes, with concise titles and clearer Persian. A matching filter button. When search is hidden, the filter button shares the tag pills' height and style.

item.title: Nex 2.5.0
item.description: More useful summaries. Keep key decisions, dates, figures and next steps in summaries suited to the content. Translation in more languages. Choose from 36 searchable languages. Long translations show progress and resume unfinished parts while Nex stays open. Comfortable reading. Expand long text-file previews and tap inline code in assistant replies to copy it. Text-selection highlights and Persian notifications are clearer. A calmer smart summary. Its border animates once per expansion and fades smoothly, without restarting when you return from a note. Clearer AI failures. Image and audio tools explain known file, connection and service failures. Calendar days work individually with TalkBack.

item.description: Habit tracking. Plan flexible schedules, track progress and streaks, and set reminders that respect completed and resting days.

item.title: Nex 2.3.6

item.title: Nex 2.3.5
item.description: Clouds that drift in. In pull to refresh, a cloud now drifts in from beyond the edge instead of appearing inside the sky, and the drift runs as one smooth, endless loop — it no longer jumps every few seconds. A copy made for Cafe Bazaar and Myket. The copy published for the stores has no in-app updater and no longer asks for permission to install apps, because the store keeps it up to date. No unencrypted connections at all. The installed app now refuses unencrypted (http) connections everywhere; the one exception, for developers' own test machines, is left in development builds only. Privacy policy brought up to date. It names Cycle as health data, says what the sponsor card is, lists the permissions as they are now, and adds how long things are kept, how they are secured, a note on children and a contact email. The same text is on the website, at DbsStudio.ir/nex/privacy.

item.title: Nex 0.7.8
item.description: The top section (the first ## heading, whatever it is titled) is exactly what release.yml publishes as the GitHub Release body — and exactly what the in-app update sheet then shows. That is the whole mechanism: no separate changelog service, no template rendered at request time. Working convention: Add each user-facing change as a short bullet under Unreleased , in the same pull request that makes the change. If it does not change anything a user would notice, it does not belong here — that is what the commit history is for. When cutting a release, rename ## Unreleased to ## vX.Y.Z (matching the tag about to be pushed) and start a fresh ## Unreleased above it for whatever comes next. release.yml refuses to publish if the top section is still literally titled Unreleased — that heading has to be renamed first, every time.
